children: Australian shares edged lower on Wednesday, heading for a fifth straight day of losses as weakness in banks outweighed a rebound in miners.
The S&P/ASX 200 index
fell 0.2% to 8,883.2 by 2304 GMT. The benchmark has shed roughly 3% in the last four sessions.
Financials

extended losses to 0.9%, a day after the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) November meeting showed policymakers felt the latest hike was necessary, with inflation risks still skewed to the upside and financial conditions not yet restrictive enough.
However, markets see the RBA's tightening cycle as nearing its end, with swaps pointing to a hold in December.
All the "Big Four" banks shed between 0.8% and 1.5%.
Investors now turn to Australian employment data due Thursday for clues on where the central bank's policy is heading.
Inflation remains the central bank's main concern, but it judges the softening labour market to be a little tight and a source of inflationary pressure.
In contrast, miners
rebounded 1.4%, on track to snap a four-day losing streak that had seen them shed more than 10%.
Mining stocks have lately been battered by weak iron ore and copper prices, as soft Chinese economic data and worries over AI spending have dampened sentiment.
Shares of sector majors BHP
and Rio Tinto
rose 1.7% and 0.1%, respectively.
Meanwhile, tech stocks
slipped as much as 2.2% to their weakest level in more than a week, tracking overnight losses in tech-heavy Nasdaq ahead of Nvidia's
earnings.

Shares of the AI chip company rose 4.5% in extended trading after it forecast sales ahead of Wall Street targets. Chairman Harvey Jones said the company would not rehire co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO.
